Subject: Recap + recommended models & quant tradeoffs for Novamed summarization POC

Hi Carmen — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and suggested plan so we’re aligned: 

What we heard
- Use case: automated clinical visit summarization (structured output; patient problem list + plan). Typical note length 300–1,200 tokens.
- Targets: 200–400ms P95 latency, sustained 40 req/s during business hours.
- Quality: factual accuracy and hallucination avoidance are top priority.
- Security: SOC 2 + US data residency required.

Recommended short list (tradeoffs included)
1) LLaMA-3-13B (instruction-tuned, private finetune option) — good accuracy/latency balance. Recommended quant: AWQ-4 for host/shared environments (best throughput with modest quality delta).
2) Mistral-7B-instruct — lower memory footprint, often slightly better factuality on short clinical prompts. Pair with GPTQ-3 if you need lower mem + conservative quality degradation.
3) Falcon-40B-instruct — high-quality baseline if you plan to run on Dedicated/Private (FP8 gives best accuracy retention but requires dedicated infra).

What AWQ / GPTQ / FP8 mean for you (executive summary)
- AWQ: reduces model size and DDR usage, gives biggest throughput uplift for hosted/dedicated mixed pools. Observed ~20–45% lower latency on 13B-class in our internal benches, with ~1–3% drop on factuality checks depending on prompt set.
- GPTQ: stable, broadly used; slightly less throughput gain vs AWQ but often similar quality.
- FP8: minimal quality delta vs fp16, but needs specialized runtime (Dedicated/Private). Best when hallucination risk cannot be tolerated.

Attachments and links
- I’ve attached the prompt set we discussed (novamed_prompt_set_v1.jsonl), and a short eval deck + preliminary bench CSV we ran against a synthetic subset. Full eval link: https://redwood.inference.company/evals/novamed/20270615

Proposed next steps
1) We run a 72-hour evaluation with your 1–2k sample notes (we’ll use your sample dataset in a redacted/controlled env). Redwood SEs will test LLaMA-3-13B (AWQ/GPTQ), Mistral-7B (GPTQ), and Falcon-40B (FP8 if you can provide Dedicated access).
2) Deep-dive call with Marissa (SE) to lock down prompt engineering, metrics (ROUGE/factuality/safe-guards), and pass/fail criteria.
3) Ben to share indicative pricing for hosted vs dedicated options and a procurement checklist.

Can you confirm: (A) sample dataset availability and preferred NDA/data transfer mechanism, and (B) who from your procurement/legal should be looped in?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync if that’s easier.

Best,

@Carmen — quick technical response to the AWQ question and proposed lightweight bench: 

On the 1–3% factuality drop: that number comes from our internal "entity-fact-check" suite (precision@entity) run on clinical-style prompts (entities = med names, dosages, problems, procedures). For LLaMA-3-13B we see:
- fp16 baseline: precision@entity = 0.942
- GPTQ-3: precision@entity = 0.935 (≈ -0.7pp)
- AWQ-4: precision@entity = 0.924 (≈ -1.8pp)

Latency (P95) on a c6g-equivalent GPU (baselines for 300-token prompts):
- LLaMA-3-13B fp16: 310 ms
- LLaMA-3-13B GPTQ: 240 ms
- LLaMA-3-13B AWQ: 180 ms
- Mistral-7B GPTQ: 165 ms
- Falcon-40B fp16 (dedicated): 270 ms (but memory and cost higher)

Tradeoff summary: AWQ gives the biggest latency win for 13B at a modest factuality delta. If your pass/fail criteria are tight (e.g., precision@entity >= 0.94), AWQ on 13B may not meet it; GPTQ on 13B or Mistral-7B (GPTQ) would be safer hosted options. FP8 on dedicated infra preserves precision similar to fp16 but requires capacity commit.

We can run the lightweight benchmark on your 500 redacted notes. For that we need: S3 link or secure Share (we can accept an encrypted transfer), a contact for access, and any PII redaction notes. Timeline: 48–72 hours from receipt of data (we’ll run the three configurations above).

I’ve attached a short CSV with the internal runs I referenced (novamed_bench_results_20270615.csv) and a short eval deck (redwood_eval_deck_2027-06.pdf).

—Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
